candidates.name: hackforla/311-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Hack for LA civic-tech project ingesting the full MyLA311 service-request feed (all LA complaint types, includes the STR/short-term-rental enforcement category as one of many) via the LA Socrata API; project states CSV and parquet snapshots are also mirrored at huggingface.co (external host, exact dataset name/size not confirmed by page content). No Airbnb-specific filtering or documentation in the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: LA is one of the three target cities (MyLA311). This is the most substantial, actively-maintained pipeline/mirror for LA's full 311 feed found; a team member would still need to filter to the STR/illegal-rental complaint category themselves to build the enforcement-activity proxy for gap area (311/STR enforcement) — not itself an Airbnb-labeled dataset.

candidates.name: ishitakapoor7/311derful
candidates.what_it_holds: Generic NYC 311 ETL tool pulling Socrata dataset erm2-nwe9 ('311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present', 22,145,244 rows, Jan 2020-Aug 2026) plus community-district boundaries (5crt-au7u); caches monthly gzipped CSVs into DuckDB. No Airbnb/STR filtering built in, but the underlying feed includes NYC's 'Illegal Home Sharing/Vacation Rental' complaint type handled by the Office of Special Enforcement, so this is a ready one-command pull method that could be filtered post-hoc.
candidates.why_useful: Point-in-time-capable, current (through Aug 2026), full-complaint-type NYC 311 pull method; fills the acquisition-method half of gap area on 311 enforcement proxies for NYC even though the repo itself does no STR-specific work.
candidates.last_activity: recent (data through Aug 2026 implies active maintenance)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partially overlaps NYC OSE registry already held (item 34, municipal STR registries) but this is the raw 311 complaint stream, a different data type

candidates.name: Haonan-100/SF311-Citizen-Service-Requests-Local-Data-Pipeline-and-Analytics
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline ingesting >7.6M San Francisco 311 service-request records (2008-2025) via the Socrata API into PostgreSQL with Metabase dashboards. Data itself is git-ignored (not committed); pipeline/config code only. Top complaint types are generic (bulky-item pickup, cleaning) with no Airbnb/STR-specific handling shown.
candidates.why_useful: SF is one of the three target cities (SF 311/OSTR). Provides a ready, long-history (17-year) one-command pull method for SF's full 311 feed, from which STR/short-term-rental complaint categories could be isolated to build an enforcement-activity proxy.
candidates.size_hint: ~7.6M rows / ~700MB CSV snapshot, not committed to repo

candidates.name: ollieiris95/nyc-311-noise-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/SQL study of NYC 311 noise complaints; committed raw file '311_noise_complaints_2024.csv' (raw_data folder) covering calendar year 2024 only, with date/time, complaint type, borough, and geolocation fields. No Airbnb or STR linkage in the documentation.
candidates.why_useful: Noise complaints are a commonly proposed proxy for short-term-rental party/turnover activity in dense neighborhoods, but this repo is single-year, city-wide (not STR-filtered) and would need substantial rework to isolate an Airbnb-adjacent signal.
candidates.size_hint: single-year CSV, row count not stated

candidates.name: GeorgiosIoannouCoder/nyc-open-data-311-service-requests
candidates.what_it_holds: Database-normalization project (third-normal-form schema) for the NYC 311 open dataset; general-purpose ETL/schema tooling, not city-specific to STR complaint types (per topic-page description only, not independently verified by full README fetch).
candidates.why_useful: Another generic NYC 311 access/normalization tool that could underlie a home-built STR/Illegal-Home-Sharing complaint-count series if someone filters the complaint-type field; marginal add over 311derful above.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps ishitakapoor7/311derful in purpose (both are generic NYC 311 pull/normalize tools)

candidates.name: rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-warehouse pipeline (Python extraction -> Snowflake -> dbt -> Metabase) combining Inside Airbnb listings (~35M records claimed, 2015-2020), Kaggle world-cities population/location data, and Numbeo cost-of-living indices via Kaggle, to study Airbnb's effect on global housing markets. No 311/complaints/enforcement data of any kind; no data committed to the repo itself (users must run the pipeline against their own Snowflake account).
candidates.why_useful: Off-theme for 311/enforcement specifically (found while searching short-term-rental topic), but flagged since it claims a much larger historical Inside Airbnb pull (2015-2020, 35M records) than what we currently hold — could be relevant to gap #1 (historical Inside Airbnb archives) even though it stores no data itself, only a reproducible pull method.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Method overlaps our existing Inside Airbnb holdings; only useful if it can independently reach pre-2023 vintages already off the CDN

candidates.name: rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs analyzing San Francisco housing vs. short-term rentals: SF City Performance Scorecard hotel-rate data (Jul 2004-May 2018), Zillow long-term rental rates (Nov 2010-Sep 2018), DataSF home-price/assessment data (2007-2016, not uploaded due to GitHub size limits, downloadable from DataSF instead), and Inside Airbnb peer-to-peer short-term-rental rates (May 2015-Dec 2017). No 311/complaints/enforcement data; explicitly notes only 3 data points exist for the STR series, limiting granularity.
candidates.why_useful: Off-theme (no complaints data) but a small, real committed SF housing-vs-STR dataset with an older Inside Airbnb slice (2015-2017) than our current holdings for that city; low value given only 3 STR data points.
candidates.size_hint: small, several CSVs; home-price file excluded for size
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps Inside Airbnb SF holdings; hotel-rate and Zillow-rental components may be new

notes: This theme came back essentially empty on GitHub for the actual intersection (Airbnb/STR + 311/noise/enforcement complaints). WebSearch's session-wide budget was already exhausted (200/200) before any query for this scout ran, so no WebSearch results at all were available. Fell back to WebFetch on search-engine result pages: DuckDuckGo html/lite both returned 403 Forbidden for every query; Google and Bing rendered but appear to serve bot-detected/cached generic SERPs (Bing repeatedly returned only Airbnb's own marketing/social pages regardless of query text or the site:github.com operator, even via the RSS output format; Google returned an empty interstitial). Mojeek returned 403. Marginalia rendered but showed only its help/filter UI, no actual hits. gh search repos (4 allowed calls plus one retry after a 403 rate-limit) returned zero results for every specific NYC/LA/SF 311+Airbnb phrase tried, and github.com/search itself hit HTTP 429 with a 3600s retry-after. The one channel that worked reliably was GitHub's static /topics/<tag> pages (topics: 311, short-term-rental, airbnb-data, vacation-rental, 311-data, illegal-hotels [empty], airbnb-nyc [empty], local-law-18 [empty], noise-complaints [empty]) plus direct repo/org URL fetches, which is how every candidate above was actually found and verified. None of roughly 60 repositories surfaced across those topic pages combine Airbnb/STR with 311/noise/complaint data; the closest matches are generic city 311 ETL/mirror tools (hackforla/311-data for LA, ishitakapoor7/311derful and GeorgiosIoannouCoder's repo for NYC, Haonan-100's for SF) that would need a team member to filter the complaint-type field to an 'Illegal Home Sharing'/STR category themselves, and two Airbnb-vs-housing studies with no complaints angle. Recommend a human either (a) rerun this theme once the shared WebSearch budget resets, since the topic-page approach is structurally limited to repos maintainers tagged correctly, or (b) treat this as a genuine gap: nobody on GitHub appears to have built or mirrored an Airbnb-enforcement 311 dataset, so the fastest path is pulling the categorized complaint type directly from NYC Open Data's erm2-nwe9 feed (or LA/SF equivalents) in-house rather than continuing to search for a pre-built one.
